difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a finite module over a Noetherian ring and a fixed positive degree, the Tor groups against the successive quotients by powers of an ideal form a strictly pro-zero system. The statement carries a literature reference with a comment on its wording, and the text supplies its own proof: for degree one the Tor group is identified with a quotient of an intersection of the kernel with a power of the ideal in a free module, and Artin-Rees bounds that intersection inside a suitable smaller power of the kernel, which is exactly the required vanishing on a tail; higher degrees are reduced to degree one by the usual dimension shift along the short exact sequence.
